title: PULSE: Using Mixed-Quality Models for Reducing Serverless Keep-Alive Cost
problem: Serverless ML inference requires fixed keep-alive policies (e.g., 10-minute strategies) to mitigate cold starts, but large model sizes cause substantial keep-alive costs and memory consumption peaks that strain resources.
motivation: Reducing keep-alive costs is critical for practical serverless ML inference deployment, as fixed policies incur significant overhead that limits cost-effectiveness.
method: PULSE makes it cheaper to keep AI models ready to use instantly by using multiple versions of each model with different quality levels. Instead of keeping one full-size model running for a fixed duration (a simple but wasteful approach), PULSE dynamically chooses which version to keep alive based on current demand—using smaller, faster models when accuracy is less critical and upgrading when needed. This approach prevents sudden memory spikes and works with existing serverless platforms' warming strategies.
key_novelty: The core idea is dynamically switching between model variants of different sizes and accuracy levels based on demand, rather than keeping one fixed-size model running for a predetermined time.
contributions: PULSE: dynamic keep-alive mechanism using model variants for cost optimization
Reduced keep-alive costs compared to fixed 10-minute policies
Optimization framework balancing costs, accuracy, and service time
Demonstrated integration improving existing serverless warm-up strategies
